label: Attenuated per se reception of esse
term: attenuated per se reception of esse
definition: AttenuatedEsseReception m w holds when the actual concreta at w are countable and there are real-valued weights wt v u >= 0, own esse s v >= 0, esse amounts P v and constants 0 <= q < 1 and M >= 0 such that: every P v is positive and at most M; each row of weights is summable with total at most q; P v <= s v + sum over u of wt v u * P u (with that sum summable); positive weight wt v u > 0 occurs only when u is an actual concrete ground of v at w; and positive own esse s u > 0 occurs only when u has no actual concrete ground. Ordinary meaning: every actual thing has some positive, bounded amount of being; what it has is at most what it has of itself plus a weighted share of what its grounds have; each act of receiving passes on at most the fraction q < 1 of the givers' being; and a thing that has some actual ground has no being of its own (intermediates contribute nothing of their own, the per se condition). Orientation (not warrant): light passed through a stack of tinted panes, each pane passing at most a fixed fraction. Network analogues of dropping single clauses (formal, existing QuantitativeTransferPaths controls on weighted networks, not Profile-level controls): without uniform loss, lossless averaging on an infinite binary tree keeps positive output with no source (binaryFixed); without the common bound, a half-loss chain with powers 2^n does (halfFixed). Distinguished from mere lossless per se transmission, which is consistent with an endless sourceless chain (INFINITE-LOCAL-TRANSMISSION-MODEL), and from a finite natural-number rank, which directly gives well-foundedness.
note: Analyst framework definition, attribution deferred (#310 model 4). The quantities have no real-world calibration, and nothing here claims that being is measured by real numbers; the uniform loss and common bound are the load-bearing, contested clauses. It composes the existing weighted-network theorem QuantitativeTransferPaths.finitePath (#1379). The per se clause (positive own esse only at roots) excludes things that have partly own and partly received being; a weaker clause is untested.
